messages:
ana: Running into 429 weirdness in async python client. It respects Retry-After but ignores X-RateLimit-Reset so clients spike when reset hits.
jorge: paste headers?
ana: example: ```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 2
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1774567320
```
ana: we sleep 2s (Retry-After) but reset is 20s away -> everyone retries repeatedly until the reset window.
jorge: Rule proposal: parse both. Prefer X-RateLimit-Reset (try int epoch, then HTTP-date) -> compute delta = reset - now; if delta>0 sleep(delta) else if Retry-After present sleep(float(retry_after)) else fallback to exp backoff + jitter.
maria: agree. Expose small util `devex.rate.parse_rate_headers` + `AsyncRateGuard.wait_if_needed(headers, now_fn=...)`. Keep public API tiny.
nana: tests: variants for epoch reset, http-date reset, only retry-after, missing headers, and conflicting values.
ci-bot: CI started for branch "devex/rl-guard" (PR 4499).
jorge: will add typing (TypedDict) and sync wrapper. maria: I'll review tests.
nana: will open PR tonight.
